text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Indonesian press on October 25. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy. Telephone: (6221) 384-6364. Fax: (6221) 344-8404.

A group linked to President Suharto has bought around a large stake in Indonesia's largest car manufacturer PT Astra Internasional. The Nusamba group, headed by timber tycoon Muhammad "Bob" Hasan, acquired the stock through the Surabaya Stock Exchange at a price of 4,100 rupiah a share.
Indonesia and Australia agreed on Thursday to establish a joint regional airline to serve the eastern islands of the Indonesian archipelago and the Australian continent.

Suharto asked for Colombia's help in keeping the issue of East Timor off the agenda of the IBOR-American conference to be held in Chile next month. Portugal, East Timor's former colonial ruler and which opposes Indonesian rule over the territory, will be attending the conference.

Guruh Sukarnoputra, brother of ousted Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) leader Megawati Sukarnoputri, has expressed a wish to join a group affiliated to the ruling political party Golkar. Guruh is a member of parliament for the PDI but has recently said he wants to move away from politics to concentrate more on his choreography.
State-owned bank Bank Negara Indonesia (BNI) will make its initial public offering at 850 rupiah a share on November 25. The shares will be offered on both the Jakarta and Surabaya Stock Exchanges.
Indonesia is expected to offer incentives to local franchisers in a bid to compete against their foreign counterparts operating in the country, the cooperatives ministery said without giving details.
